item.title: Trump threatens Oman, Iran war in stalemate as 60-day talks window ends
item.description: The 60-day deadline for the U.S. and Iran to negotiate a peace deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz is expiring, with no agreement in sight.

item.title: Tupac Shakur was murdered in "act of revenge," prosecutor tells jury
item.description: The long-unsolved drive-by shooting gripped the hip-hop community, partly because no one was charged until Duane "Keffe D" Davis was indicted in 2023.

item.title: Penn State frat brothers charged with running cocaine trafficking ring
item.description: Two Penn State fraternities are at the center of a cocaine trafficking ring bust, leading to charges against 14 people, authorities said.

item.title: Hawaii slowly begins cleanup process after Lala slams state
item.description: Lala battered Hawaii as a hurricane, bringing heavy rain, damaging winds and mudslides. CBS News' Jonathan Vigliotti has more.

item.title: Blanche refuses to pledge Justice Department independence from White House
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche is refusing to put up a wall between the Justice Department and the executive branch. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Judge blocks plan to move FBI headquarters to Reagan Building
item.description: U.S. District Judge Theodore Chuang ruled that the Trump administration's move to divert funding and cancel a plan to move the FBI to Maryland was "arbitrary and capricious and not in accordance with law."

item.title: Hayden Panettiere remembered by co-stars and friends after her death
item.description: Co-stars and friends of Hayden Panettiere​ are remembering her for her friendship, intelligence and talent after her shocking death on Sunday.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere, known for "Heroes" and "Remember the Titans," dies at 36
item.description: Hayden Panettiere, who starred in "Remember the Titans" as a child actor and rose to fame in the series "Heroes," has died at the age of 36. The coroner's office says she was found in cardiac arrest.

item.title: Key moments from the Lindsay Clancy trial as the defense starts to make its case
item.description: Lindsay Clancy has pleaded not guilty to murdering her children, but her attorneys don't deny that she caused the deaths of 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan.

item.title: Where things stand in the Iran war, 60 days after memorandum of understanding
item.description: It has been 60 days since the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding that called for negotiations to reach a larger peace deal. Despite that, the war continues. CBS News national security contributor Joseph Zacks has more.

item.title: Former Hurricane Lala drenches Hawaii, flash floods sweep away Big Island homes
item.description: Lala was weakening but still packing a punch as it moved away from the islands, forecasters said.

item.title: Gray skies turn bright yellow after lightning strike causes gas tanks to explode in Oklahoma
item.description: Lightning struck a natural gas tank south of Tulsa, Oklahoma, sparking a massive fire that spread to nearby tanks. Jason Allen has new developments.

item.title: After a mother went missing in Las Vegas, her family received texts from her phone
item.description: After a 63-year-old woman in Las Vegas didn't return from a trip to the drugstore, her family said they started getting text messages from the woman's phone. The family spoke with Nicole Valdes.

item.title: How economic conditions are fueling a rise of U.S. socialism
item.description: A new CBS News poll shows 58% of Democrats have a positive view of socialism while 50% have a negative view of capitalism. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto and Fin Gómez have more.

item.title: Trump takes aim at longtime ally Oman as Strait of Hormuz remains gridlocked
item.description: With no deal in sight to end the conflict in Iran or reopen the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices are up once again. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Details as Lindsay Clancy's mom and sister take the stand
item.description: The defense began its work on Monday in the case of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman on trial for killing her three children. Her mother and sister took the stand and Shanelle Kaul has the details.

item.title: 14 charged in alleged Penn State cocaine ring
item.description: Thirteen former and current Penn State students, and one student's father, are facing charges related to an alleged cocaine ring. Prosecutors allege drugs were cut and packaged at two frat houses, sometimes by pledges. Michael George reports.

item.title: Indiana inundated with historic flooding, more than 100,000 without power
item.description: Flooding continued to inundate parts of the central and southern regions of Indiana on Monday. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Hawaii reels in the aftermath of Hurricane Lala
item.description: The eye of Lala passed just 30 miles off the Big Island of Hawaii's coast over the weekend, but it was the rain that caused catastrophe for its residents. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

item.title: Hollywood grieves Hayden Panettiere as authorities investigate her death at 36
item.description: With no signs of foul play or trauma, authorities said the investigation into actor Hayden Panettiere's death is just beginning. The former child star was on "Guiding Light" and also had breakout roles in "Heroes" and "Nashville." She died at 36 years old. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: First witnesses speak in Tupac Shakur's long-awaited murder trial
item.description: Opening statements were delivered in Tupac Shakur's long-awaited murder trial on Monday. Nearly 30 years ago, the iconic rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas, a pivotal moment in music history. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman reports.

item.title: U.S. and Iran's 60-day MOU expires: What this means, what Trump wants
item.description: Monday marked the end of the 60-day negotiation period outlined in the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran. CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes has more as the war shows no signs of slowing down.

item.title: Why Trump ordered U.S. military to reduce exercises with South Korea
item.description: President Trump has ordered the Pentagon to scale back its joint military exercises with South Korea after he said the country declined to join the U.S.'s efforts to denuclearize Iran. CBS News Pentagon reporter Eleanor Watson has more details.

item.title: What the emojis you use say about how old you are
item.description: A new New York Times report has found that your choice in emojis could give some insight into your age and demographic. Eve Washington, the writer of the piece, joined "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Baby with heart defect at center of surrogate dispute receives first surgery
item.description: The baby was born with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, which requires a series of surgeries. The parents had asked the surrogate to get an abortion when they learned of the diagnosis.

item.title: Luigi Mangione's New York trial delayed
item.description: Luigi Mangione's New York state trial on second-degree murder charges is being delayed.

item.title: 8/17: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Iran war continues 60 days after memorandum of understanding signed; Florida primaries on Tuesday.

item.title: Hegseth to go to Iowa to campaign for GOP candidates, sources say
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was scheduled to head to Iowa on Monday to give remarks, speak to veterans and campaign, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Has your license plate been tracked by Flock? Here's how to check.
item.description: The website​ HaveIBeenFlocked has compiled a database of 4.6 million license plate records that have appeared in roughly 242 million Flock searches.

item.title: Senior Israeli official calls for killing of "30 to 40" Gazans every night
item.description: Israel's far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir calls for nightly "targeted assassinations" in Gaza: "They're not even people."
